title: Perturbation-driven quant impact orchestrator and threshold auto-calibrator
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Goal: Build an orchestrator that runs targeted perturbation experiments whenever a quantization profile, model variant (AWQ/GPTQ), or runtime config changes and then auto-calibrates per-route thresholds used by the rollout gate. We want to detect semantic quality regressions for int8/int4 modes and recommend automatic or manual rollbacks. This should be safe to run on CI for PRs and as a lightweight smoke suite in staging and can be scheduled for periodic drift scans in production cohorts.

Scope: 1) A perturbation job generator that synthesizes small, semantically-relevant perturbations (paraphrase substitutions, token deletions, numeric edge cases) per route and interrogates the quantized model variant. 2) A scoring pipeline that computes a normalized quality delta across metrics (exact-match when applicable, embedding cosine on reference responses, reranker-based rank-drop, and proprietary semantic similarity score). 3) A Bayesian threshold auto-calibrator that recommends per-route tolerances and a global budget; stores output in the manifest used by rollout gates. 4) Orchestration glue to run experiments on PRs, scheduled runs, and on-demand from Console with links to dashboards and diffs.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement the rollout plumbing itself or production forced rollbacks — those are separate (see ENG-771890). It also does not add new observability UIs beyond links to the Grafana panels created by the pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Perturbation job generator can produce at least 5 perturbation families per route (paraphrase, token deletion, numeric-edge, punctuation variants, adversarial synonyms).
End-to-end pipeline runs on a sample PR and produces a report within 45 minutes for a 200-sample route test on a single dedicated CPU job.
Auto-calibrator returns a recommended per-route threshold and a confidence score; thresholds are persisted as JSON manifest and consumable by the rollout gate.
A human review flow exists: reports link to representative failing examples + model outputs for manual triage (Confluence PR-linked document).
Integration test: when run against a benign model change, false-positive rate must be < 2% on heldout production-quality prompts.
Documentation page (Confluence) describing methodology, controls, and how to interpret the confidence score is published.
implementation_notes:
Design choices: use a hybrid metric stack (embedding cosine + rank-drop + BLEU-like token overlap for deterministic tasks). We will prioritize semantic metrics over token-level for open generation routes. Perturbation families are seeded from recent top-traffic prompts and token-distribution hotspots from the prefix/KV cache profiler.

Calibration approach: run a Bayesian optimizer (small budget, sequential) to pick the threshold that balances false positives vs false negatives using a small holdout validation set per route. Store per-route ROC-like curve snapshots for future threshold adjustments.

Compute/Cost: default scheduled runs will target 5% of production routes nightly; heavier full-cohort scans scheduled weekly for high-SLA customers only. To reduce GPU time, quant inference for these jobs will run on dedicated CPU fallback runtime for small sample sets and on low-priority GPU pool for heavy scans.

Data handling: retain raw transcripts and diff artifacts for 30 days in S3; only aggregate scores and thresholds are stored in the manifest service longer-term. Ensure PII scrubber runs on captured prompts before storage.

Rollout interaction: the manifest produced will be versioned and tagged with the PR/commit; the rollout gate references manifest version for decisions. The orchestrator will include a simulated-impact mode that emits expected request-level failures without modifying traffic.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12 - Asha: Created ticket and initial design sketch. Spike planned to evaluate perturbation generator approaches (paraphrase models vs rule-based).

2026-02-18 - Ethan: Ran spike comparing paraphrase generation with supervised synonym replacement. Paraphrase model produced higher semantic variance but introduced hallucination noise; decided to use hybrid approach (rule-filter + paraphrase ensemble).
2026-02-25 - Team: Prototype perturbation generator implemented; initial harness can run 3 families and persist artifacts to s3://redwood-quant-evals/dev/ENG-128004/

2026-03-02 - QA: End-to-end smoke on staging (100-sample route) completed. Observed two routes with consistent semantic score drops when switching to AWQ-int4 variant. Filed follow-ups to investigate layerwise sensitivity (ENG-502401).

2026-03-05 - Design review: PM and Design reviewed report format. Requested explicit representative example blocks near top of report and clearer troubleshooting hints. Implemented changes to report renderer.

2026-03-09 - Ethan: Integrated Bayesian optimizer (open-source library) and added persistence for recommended thresholds; first auto-calibration run produced per-route thresholds with confidence metric. Running extended validation against heldout corpus this week.
review_feedback: PM (Jorge Martinez): Ensure threshold recommendations include expected economic impact (estimated delta tokens cost when forcing fallback).
Security (Leah Chen): Confirm PII scrub pipeline is applied before anything written to long-term storage; add security checklist to Confluence page.
Infra (Ravi Patel): For nightly runs, avoid saturating the low-priority GPU pool; we should queue jobs and collect telemetry to throttle concurrently running scans.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Auto-calibrator overfits on synthetic perturbations -> Mitigation: require a heldout human-labeled validation set and cap automatic rollout changes unless confidence > 0.9.
Risk: High compute cost if many routes flagged -> Mitigation: per-route budget; start with top-5% traffic and use sampling; offer full-scan only for paid customers.
Risk: False positives disrupting rollouts -> Mitigation: default to recommend-only mode; only enable enforced blocklists after manual approval.
next_steps: Finish heldout validation and compute false-positive rate across 12 routes (assigned to Ethan, due 2026-03-14).
Add economic impact estimator to the report (token delta + expected rollout cost).
Hook the manifest writer into the rollout gate API for simulated-impact mode (integration with ENG-771890).
Schedule a cross-team demo for runtime-1.28 release sync and get approval for enabling nightly lightweight scans.
